positioning: The dog that does everything and still just wants to please you.
story: The Labrador never set foot in Labrador. It grew up on the docks of Newfoundland, where fishermen kept a short-coated water dog to haul nets and fetch fish that slipped the line.

British sportsmen watched it work. They shipped a few home in the 1800s and bred the finest gun dog in the field. The job left its mark. Webbed feet. A thick otter tail for a rudder. A coat that beads water like a raincoat.
Almost anything you ask of a Lab, it does well and gladly. Labs guide the blind and hear for the deaf. They sniff out explosives and the early warning of a seizure. They pull children from pools.
The genius is the mouth. A Lab can carry a raw egg across a yard and set it down without a dent. Add a bottomless wish to please and you get a dog that is almost embarrassingly easy to teach.
Off duty, it is pure appetite and affection. It will eat what it should not. It will lean its full weight on your leg. It will treat every visitor as a friend it has not met yet.
America agreed for thirty-one years in a row. The Lab was the No. 1 breed from 1991 to 2021, and it is still No. 2. Gentle, tireless, and sure the next good thing is coming. Usually it involves food.
fblocks: A geographic mix-up that stuck. The breed descends from the St. John’s water dog of Newfoundland. British breeders named it for the wrong coast.
Endal, a British assistance dog who loaded washing machines. Jake, a search dog at Ground Zero. Zanjeer, who found explosives in Mumbai, 1993.
Bred to work all day, so a bored Lab invents its own job. Many carry a hunger gene, so portions matter. The coat sheds.
A dense, water-repellent double coat in black, yellow, or chocolate, all in one litter. The otter tail steers like a rudder.
About seven puppies to a litter. Recognized by the AKC in 1917. No. 1 in America for thirty-one years.
days: A screened porch, a daybed, and a paperback. The dog is saving the spot.
Labs have webbed toes and an otter tail. Both help them swim.
Endal, a British assistance dog, could load a washing machine and use a cash machine.
A Lab litter can hold black, yellow, and chocolate puppies. Three colors, one family.
Check the bucket. Check the dock. Most days the best thing is just beyond your nose.
Labs held the No. 1 spot in America for thirty-one years. Then came the Frenchie.
Puppies piled in a red wagon beside the lake. All the way down to the dock and back.
last_walk:
The lights come on along the dock, and the lake goes pink.
Hank and old Tucker walk toward the water, side by side. The young dog slows for the old one. A Lab knows this part by heart. The long day ends at the edge of the lake, and the lake is still.
